title: Tech 10 Data Reconciliation
decision: Choose a consistency and reconciliation strategy for conflicting replicated records.
context: Two regional systems can accept updates during network partitions.
Records contain user profile fields and an account status field.
Conflicts are rare but can affect authorization if handled incorrectly.
constraints: Account status must never be downgraded from suspended to active by stale data.
Normal profile-field conflicts should converge automatically.
The system must remain writable during a regional partition.
options: Use last-write-wins for every field based on wall-clock timestamp.
Use field-specific merge rules with monotonic status precedence and version metadata.
Disable writes in one region whenever connectivity is uncertain.

evidence.fact: Clock skew between regions has reached 47 seconds during past incidents.
Profile conflicts occur in about 0.03 percent of multi-region edits.
Account status transitions have a defined precedence where suspended must dominate active until an explicit reviewed unsuspend action.
Both regions already attach unique operation ids to writes.
Business continuity requires both regions to accept profile updates during a partition lasting up to one hour.
Conflict-resolution code can distinguish explicit reviewed unsuspend operations from ordinary profile updates.
